findings.claim: The doc comment of topicMadeOnAMainMerge says it returns three commits (M, the first commit of topic and the merge of main into topic), but the function returns four: m, first, merged and tip. The comment does not describe the signature.
proof_refs: fix1.diff lines 92-97 (comment) and 97 (signature `(m, first, merged, tip string)`)

findings.claim: The unit tests cover only the IsAncestor failure and the no-ancestry call on a chain that reaches the base. The two-step decision in startsInBase (start in base and oldest not in base) is never asserted in the app package with fakeGit. It is covered only by command-level tests over real repositories. A mutation that swaps the `want` values or drops the oldest check is caught only by the existing 'a range that begins before the base' subtest. I could not run any test.

evidence: Read the full diff and the criteria S1-S3 and L3 in odd/tasks/review-chain-integration-base.md.

Read engine/review/app/chain.go at head. The done rule matches S1 and S2. IsAncestor is asked only when start differs from the base and is not empty. A git failure is wrapped under the 'the chain from ... to ...' prefix. insideRange returns the oldest covered commit (the one whose first parent is start).

Read gitexec.IsAncestor (engine/review/gitexec/gitexec.go:781-798). It requires full object names, treats exit code 1 with empty output as false, and any other error as an error, so the chain refuses and does not clear.
Checked the existing straddle case by reasoning. If the base lies strictly inside a range, oldest is an ancestor of the base, so startsInBase returns false and the refusal is kept (S2).
Not run: go test, go vet and the CLI. All conclusions come from reading the code.
